transcript.content: Hi, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, it's nice to meet you too. Thanks for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place. 

I guess... well, I work in landscaping, just a regular crew guy, you know? But recently, I kind of... I don't know, I just got really, really into this new idea. I started trying to run three different bids at once, and I was calling city officials, lining up plant suppliers, just... doing a lot. I guess I was messaging everyone I knew about this big park idea I had. It was like I couldn't shut it off, if that makes sense? 

I just wanted to do a really good job, but my boss seemed kind of worried, so... here I am. Is that the kind of thing you need to know?
During this time, have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Um, sleep? No, I don't think so. I mean, I was definitely staying busy, maybe up a little late a couple nights sketching out some of the planting layouts, but... I wasn't staying up all night or anything bad like that. 

I still got my rest. I always try to make sure I'm rested enough for the crew the next day, you know? I don't want to be a drag on the guys. So, yeah, I'd say I was sleeping pretty normal, just regular hours. Is... is that okay? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don't?

Oh, um, no. No, definitely not. I haven't... I don't see things or hear voices or anything like that. I mean, I know sometimes people do, and I'm not judging or anything, but... no, not me. 

My hearing and everything is totally fine. I promise I'm completely normal in that department. Is... is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During this time, did you feel more important or more capable than usual?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound full of myself, because I promise I'm not usually like that. I always try to just keep my head down and work hard. But... yeah, I guess for a little while there, I did feel pretty capable. 

I honestly believed I was about to become, like, the guy, you know? The main person that every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping. I was just so sure I could pull it all off and handle these massive projects. Which is... well, it's kind of embarrassing to admit out loud now, since I'm really just trying to keep my small jobs paid up and stay on top of things at work. 

I just thought I was onto something really good that could help the community, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound arrogant or anything. Is... is it normal to get a little carried away with a good idea like that?
Around the time this started, had you been using any drugs like meth or cocaine?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I've never touched anything like meth or cocaine, I promise you. I know sometimes guys in landscaping or construction can get mixed up in that kind of stuff to keep their energy up for the long shifts, but... I swear I stay far away from all of that. 

I just... I really wouldn't want to mess up my job or get in trouble, you know? I hope you don't think I'm the kind of guy who would do those things. I just drink my regular coffee in the mornings, I swear. Is... is that what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth and not making you think badly of me.
During that time, did you have any beliefs that other people said were unrealistic or not true?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, my friends thought I was biting off way more than I could chew with the whole sustainable landscaping empire idea, and they definitely told me to slow down. But I didn't think anything... crazy. 

I know some people get really out there with conspiracy theories or thinking they have superpowers or whatever, but I've never been like that. I just thought I had a really solid business plan, even if I was maybe a little too eager about it. 

I always try to stay pretty grounded, you know? I hope that makes sense. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Did this period get you into serious trouble at work or with money?

Well, um... I wouldn't say *serious* trouble at work. I still have my job, and I'm a really hard worker, I promise. But... money-wise... 

Gosh, it's really embarrassing to admit this. I just... I got so ahead of myself with that whole landscaping empire idea. I ended up putting a lot of things on a credit card. Just, you know, new tools, a bunch of plants, some nicer work clothes so I'd look professional, and even some local ads. I was just operating like... like the money from those big jobs was already coming in, you know? 

And now... I look at the balance and I honestly just feel sick. Because I really can't cover it on my normal paycheck right now. 

I'm usually so responsible with my finances, I swear. I hate that I let this happen, and I'm going to pick up extra shifts to fix it, I promise. I hope... I hope you don't think I'm just some reckless guy who throws money away. Is it... is it common for people to make a mistake like that when they get too excited about a project?
During that period, were you talking much more than usual or feeling like you couldn't stop talking?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I was just really passionate about all the ideas I had, you know? 

I guess... I might have been talking a bit faster than normal, just because I wanted to get everything out before I forgot it. My mom did tell me to take a breath a few times when I was explaining the business plan to her. But I wasn't, like, rambling or anything crazy. I just had a lot to say and I was excited. 

I really try to be a good listener, too, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who just talks over everyone else. I know that's really rude. Does... does that make sense? Being a little more chatty just because you're excited about something?
During that time, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Well, um... happy might not be the exact right word. It was more like... I just felt really fired up, you know? Like I was almost... bigger than myself, if that makes sense. Like I could take on the world. 

I guess I felt really good about things, mostly. But, um... I did get a little... well, I guess I could get a little easily frustrated, too. Like, if one of the guys at work questioned my plan or told me I needed to slow down, I... I might have snapped at them. 

I feel really bad about it now, because I'm usually a really easygoing guy, I promise. I don't like conflict at all. But I just reacted way harder than made sense for the situation. I've apologized to them since then, of course. I just... I don't want you to think I'm an angry person. Is it normal to feel really great but also kind of irritable at the same time?
About how long did this fired-up period last?

Um, well, let's see... I think it was right around the time I started, you know, completely remaking my whole approach for that big city park pitch. I just felt so driven to get it perfect. 

I guess that whole stretch, where I was feeling so... confident and energized, it probably lasted for about two weeks? And then... well, then I just kind of crashed really hard. 

But I mean, two weeks isn't that long, right? I'm sure a lot of guys get really focused on a big project for a couple of weeks and put everything into it. It's just that the crash afterward was... it was tough. I really try to be steady and reliable, I swear I do. I hate letting people down when I lose my energy like that. Does that sound like a normal amount of time to be focused on something before you just run out of steam?
After that fired-up period ended, did you go through a stretch where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... yeah. Yes, I did. I really hate admitting it, because I don't want you to think I'm just making excuses or being lazy. I always try to pull my weight and do a good job. 

But, um... the truth is, that depressed feeling... it's actually been hanging over me for about a year now. I've been trying so hard to just push through it and, you know, be positive. But this latest crash, after all that energy faded... it's definitely the worst it's gotten. 

I try my absolute best to hide it from the other guys on the crew, I promise. I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down. Is it... does that happen to other people? Being stuck in a rut for a whole year, even when you're trying your absolute hardest to just snap out of it?
During that depressed stretch, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess so, yeah. I mean, I still try to keep busy, you know? I don't want to just sit around doing nothing. But... 

Like, usually, on my days off, I love going hiking. I'd take my camera out and just spend hours taking pictures of creek beds and the trees, trying to catch the light just right. It always helped me clear my head. 

But lately... I don't know. I just haven't had it in me. I'll drive out there, but I just end up leaving my camera in the truck. I just don't really care if the light is perfect anymore, or... or about taking pictures at all, really. 

I feel awful about it, honestly. I know I should be out there enjoying nature, getting exercise... I'm really trying to get back into it, I promise. I don't want to be someone who just gives up on their hobbies. Do you think... is it normal to just lose your spark for stuff like that when you're feeling down?
During that fired-up period, were you hospitalized because of it?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. 

I mean, I know I said I was really driven and maybe a little intense about the park pitch, but I was still going to work every day and doing my job. I wasn't... I wasn't out of control or doing anything crazy that would make someone want to lock me up, I swear. 

I just had a lot of energy, you know? Like I drank too much coffee. But I was still being responsible. I would never want to cause that kind of trouble or make anyone worry about me like that. That's not the kind of guy I am. Does that make sense? Like, you can be really focused and energized without it being, like, a hospital kind of thing, right?

Like, usually, on my days off, I love going hiking. I'd take my camera out and just spend hours taking pictures of creek beds and the trees, trying to catch the light just right. It always helped me clear my head. 

But lately... I don't know. I just haven't had it in me. I'll drive out there, but I just end up leaving my camera in the truck. I just don't really care if the light is perfect anymore, or... or about taking pictures at all, really. 

I feel awful about it, honestly. I know I should be out there enjoying nature, getting exercise... I'm really trying to get back into it, I promise. I don't want to be someone who just gives up on their hobbies. Do you think... is it normal to just lose your spark for stuff like that when you're feeling down?

patient.answer:
Oh, no, no, definitely not. I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. 

I mean, I know I said I was really driven and maybe a little intense about the park pitch, but I was still going to work every day and doing my job. I wasn't... I wasn't out of control or doing anything crazy that would make someone want to lock me up, I swear. 

I just had a lot of energy, you know? Like I drank too much coffee. But I was still being responsible. I would never want to cause that kind of trouble or make anyone worry about me like that. That's not the kind of guy I am. Does that make sense? Like, you can be really focused and energized without it being, like, a hospital kind of thing, right?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct approximately 2-week period of elevated/expansive and irritable mood with increased goal-directed activity, grandiosity, increased talkativeness, and excessive spending causing financial consequences, without psychosis, hospitalization, or decreased need for sleep. This supports a hypomanic episode rather than full mania. He also reports a depressive syndrome with depressed mood and anhedonia persisting about a year and worsening after the hypomanic period. The combination is most consistent with bipolar II disorder.
